Marta: heads-up — after landing the new FP8 per-channel kernels I see a consistent perf regression on long-prefix streams (8–12% slower p50 token latency) when KV cache is warm. Not sure if kernel selection or cache alignment is the culprit :thinking:
Kevin: do you have a quick profile / numbers? is this across batch sizes or only certain shapes?
Marta: quick numbers from yesterday's perf run (model: rdx-large, seq_len 2048 prefix + 1024 decode):
```
baseline (fp16): p50=92ms p95=220ms, tokens/sec=145
new fp8-per-channel kernels: p50=100ms p95=240ms, tokens/sec=128
4-bit mixed fallback (small batches): p50=110ms
```
These are with batch=1 and batch=8. regression is worse with larger prefix sequences.
Sasha: did the calibration dataset include long conversational prefixes? many of our calibrations are decoder-only and miss attention-key distribution when cache is hot.
Marta: good point — we used the usual 5k decode-only samples. I re-ran a small calibration with 1k long-prefix examples and the FP8 kernel p50 dropped ~3% but still worse than fp16.
Arjun: could be a kernel selection artifact: when prefix-length crosses certain multiples we end up using a different attention kernel that isn't optimized for quantized matmuls + kv-accum. Also per-channel quantization on attention k/v matrices can be sensitive to outliers introduced by long contexts.
Trish: batching heuristics also matter — continuous batching merges requests differently when cache entries are reused; that can change memory alignment and trigger a non-quantized path in the runtime. Any traces showing which kernels are chosen?
deploy-bot: profiling run uploaded: https://ci.redwood.ai/prof/2026-03-10-0423 (flame graph + kernel selection CSV) :eyes:
Kevin: ok, looking at the CSV — I see attention path switching between kernel_v1_quant and kernel_v2_fp_fallback around prefix lengths ~512/1536. Looks deliberate (heuristic threshold) but maybe we need a quant-aware threshold.
Sasha: on the quant side — per-channel vs per-tensor: per-channel usually preserves more dynamic range for outliers but makes the runtime heavier. For 4-bit and FP8 we saw that per-tensor clipping (with robust outlier handling) sometimes gives better memory locality and faster GEMM kernels.
Marta: tradeoff: per-channel reduces quality drop in a lot of cases, but per-channel also has more variance in scaling factors across rows which hurts fused kernels that assume uniform scale.
Arjun: proposal: split calibration by operator class. Use per-tensor for attention QKV matmuls (helps fused attention kernels), per-channel for FFN dense and layernorm-affine weights. Also, run calibration with simulated kv-cache warmup (i.e., include prefix state in activation collection).
Trish: +1. We should also standardize outlier handling: trim top/bottom 0.1% of activations per-tensor before computing scale, and run a Hampel filter pass to catch isolated spikes. That reduces per-channel scale variance.
Kevin: how big should the calibration set be? current defaults are 5k decodes.
Sasha: from experiments: 2k diverse samples with 80/20 split short/long covers distribution well for perf matrices. For safety run a 10k run once per major model change.
Marta: measured effect: run A (decoder-only 5k) = baseline above; run B (2k mixed with prefix sim) lowered p50 by 3% for FP8-per-channel; run C (2k + trimming outliers) lowered further 2%. Still occasional spikes p95.
Arjun: spikes likely due to kernel fallback path triggering on certain batch alignments. We should add unit tests that exercise boundary prefix lengths for kernel thresholds.
Trish: also validate batching heuristics — when small continuous batches form we currently fall back to reference GEMM for correctness. Maybe we can relax correctness checks for quantized path if we have stronger numerics tests.
Kevin: action items?
Marta: I'll assemble a calibration dataset: 2k samples, sampling 80% short (<=128 prefix tokens) and 20% long (>1024), ensure sources include code, docs, conversational logs. Save as `quant-cali/2k-prefix-mix-2026-03.jsonl`. I'll run per-operator calibration passes (per-tensor for attn, per-channel for FFN) with trimming 0.1% and a Hampel filter. I'll attach results here.
Arjun: I'll add kernel-selection trace logs to the perf harness and create test cases at the 512/1536 boundaries.
Sasha: I'll run quality checks (logprobs + ROUGE on eval prompts) to confirm no regression from trimming.
Trish: I'll run a batching stress test to produce alignment cases where the runtime previously took fallback.
Kevin: timeline?
Marta: aim to have initial results in 48 hours, follow-up A/B runs next week. I'll open a GH issue and tag the experiment `quant-mix-expt-1873`.
Sasha: quick note — for reproducibility include random seeds and sample provenance in the dataset metadata. Also log whether we simulated kv-cache warm or used real prefix state.
Marta: will do. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
Kevin: thanks — this covers both perf and quant tradeoffs. We'll iterate after the experiment. :rocket:
